explanation: Motion problems use TIME as the parameter: the horizontal position grows steadily at v cos(theta) while the vertical position rises and falls under gravity. Split the launch speed into components — slide the angle and watch how a steeper angle trades horizontal range for height. The violet arrow is the live velocity vector (it tips downward as gravity slows the rise and speeds the fall), and the green dot marks where the path lands when y returns to 0. Change speed and g to see the whole arc reshape.
bullets: Time t is the parameter; x and y are separate functions of the same t.
Horizontal motion is constant (v cos theta); vertical motion is accelerated by gravity.
Flight time is 2 v sin(theta)/g, and range = v cos(theta) times that flight time.
